data.title: Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience
data.summary: p CISA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre), and partners are releasing joint guidance, a href="https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/managing-ai-token-consumption-operational-resilience-itsm00125" target="_blank" em Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience /em /a , to help organizations understand and manage token usage in support of operations. As organizations adopt third-party super intelligence (SI) services, token-based usage models can affect cost, performance, and access to critical services. Unmanaged token consumption may contribute to rising and unpredictable costs, reduced service availability, degraded performance, token exhaustion, and denial-of-tokens or denial-of-wallet attacks. data.title: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching
data.summary: p strong Update October 23, 2026 /strong : /p p em CISA has updated this Alert to: (1) provide a SIGMA detection rule to help identify potentially suspicious activity; (2) incorporate partner resources; and (3) reinforce existing mitigation guidance. /em /p h2 strong Purpose /strong /h2 p CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a href="https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109618" CVE-2026-109618 /a and a href="https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109619" CVE-2026-109619 /a . data.title: CISA Urges Patching Critical Vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support
data.summary: p CISA is aware of critical authentication bypass vulnerability a href="https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-102764" target="_blank" CVE-2026-102764 /a , affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) versions 26.2.3 and earlier. Patches are available for supported versions (24.3.1 and later); organizations using older versions must upgrade first. Cyber threat actors are actively exploiting the vulnerability to gain initial access, then establishing persistence, escalating privileges, and moving laterally. CISA added CVE-2026-102764 to its a href="https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog" Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog /a on Oct. 16, 2026. /p p CISA urges organizations with affected self-hosted Remote Support appliances to immediately take the following actions: /p ol li Apply the BT26-05-RS patch, as outlined in BeyondTrust’s a href="https://www.beyondtrust.com/trust-center/security-advisories/bt26-05" target="_blank" Security Advisory B
